deep.reconstruction:
The page continues from the previous one. There Grothendieck identified the Hilbert tensor product L^2(mu) (x)^(2) E with L^2_E(mu), and defined, for Hilbert spaces E and F, the map from the algebraic tensor product Ebar (x) F to finite-rank operators E -> F by (abar (x) b)x = (x,a) b.

On this page he rewrites the defining formula (14) intrinsically as (15): (u x, y) = (u, xbar (x) y). The right side is the scalar product in the pre-Hilbert space Ebar (x) F. The formula also shows that u -> u-tilde is linear.

Cauchy-Schwarz then gives |(ux,y)| <= ||u||_2 ||xbar (x) y||_2 = ||u||_2 ||x|| ||y||. So the operator norm satisfies ||u-tilde|| <= ||u||_2. The map Ebar (x) F -> L(E,F) therefore extends by continuity to a linear map of norm <= 1 on the completed Hilbert tensor product Ebar (x)^(2) F.

The extension is injective. Take orthonormal bases (e_i) of E, whose conjugates form an orthonormal basis of Ebar, and (f_j) of F. Then Ebar (x)^(2) F is identified with l^2(I x J), via the identification l^2(I) (x)^(2) l^2(J) = l^2(I x J) from the previous page. The operator defined by u has matrix coefficients u_ij, so u = 0 if its operator is 0.

Definition 2 then defines Hilbert-Schmidt operators E -> F as the linear maps defined by elements of Ebar (x)^(2) F. The next page names this space L^2(E,F) and states ||u||_inf <= ||u||_2, compactness, the ideal property, the adjoint property, and the characterisation by singular values and trace.

This is a careful expository development of Hilbert-Schmidt operators as the Hilbert-space tensor product. It belongs to Grothendieck's 1953 functional-analysis notes, consistent with the preparation of his tensor-product and nuclear-space work and of his lecture notes.
errors: No mathematical errors. The check (abar (x) b, xbar (x) y) = (abar, xbar)(b,y) = (x,a)(b,y) = (ux,y) is consistent with the convention in (14).
A minor slip of the pen: after 'de norme <= 1 de Ebar (x)^(2) F' the target 'dans L(E,F)' is omitted. It is understood from the preceding sentence.

ideas.what: Identification of the completed Hilbert tensor product Ebar (x)^(2) F with the space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators E -> F, via (ux,y) = (u, xbar (x) y)
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert-Schmidt operators as Hilbert tensor product, S_2(E,F) = Ebar (x)_2 F
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schmidt (1907) for integral operators; abstract form by von Neumann, and by Murray-von Neumann (1936) and Schatten (1940s)
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Memoirs AMS 16, 1955); Résumé de la théorie métrique (1953/56)

ideas.what: Norm estimate ||u||_op <= ||u||_2 and extension by continuity
Injectivity via orthonormal bases: the matrix coefficients u_ij lie in l^2(I x J)
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert-Schmidt norm as l^2 norm of matrix entries

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook material on Hilbert-Schmidt operators, presented in Grothendieck's tensor-product language. It is cleanly done but entirely classical, and it is subsumed by his published Produits tensoriels topologiques.
transcription_corrections: 'il est trivial que l'opération définie par u a les coefficients' should likely read 'l'opérateur défini par u a pour coefficients (u_ij)'.
In 'se prolonge par continuité en une application linéaire continue de [-Ebar (x)-] norme <= 1 de Ebar (x)^(2) F', the struck fragment is a false start of 'Ebar (x)^(2) F'.
The archive page stamp at the bottom left reads '53'.
